string.text: {=taom_str_culture_description.empire}The Dunlendings, fierce hillmen of the western highlands, are a proud and ancient people. Resentful of the Rohirrim, they are known for their guerilla tactics and tenacity in battle. United under strong leaders, they fight for their survival and to reclaim the lands they believe are rightfully theirs.

{=taom_str_culture_description.vlandia}The Rohirrim, known as the Horse-lords, are the proud and noble people of Rohan, a realm of wide open plains and rolling hills. They are renowned for their skill as riders and their unmatched cavalry, which forms the backbone of their military strength. Living in a tightly-knit feudal society, the Rohirrim are led by a king and a loyal nobility who are bound by honor and tradition to protect their land and people. They are fiercely independent, valuing freedom above all, and their warriors are trained to fight with spears, swords, and bows, all while astride their powerful steeds.

{=taom_str_culture_description.battania}The Variags of Khand are a ruthless and warlike people from the eastern steppes. Known for their mastery of horses and deadly chariots, they bring a unique and brutal style of warfare. Aligned with Sauron, the Variags fight for power and plunder, spreading fear across Middle-earth.

{=taom_str_culture_description.khuzait}The Easterlings are a proud and disciplined people, hailing from the vast eastern lands beyond Mordor. Renowned for their resilience and mastery of warfare, they are both farmers and warriors, blending agrarian traditions with a fierce martial culture. Their armies are known for their fearsome cavalry, adorned in ornate armor and carrying deadly spears and bows. With a rich heritage of craftsmanship and loyalty to their kin, the Easterlings march to war under vibrant banners of gold and crimson, striking fear into the hearts of their enemies. Their allegiance to Sauron has made them a formidable force, uniting under his shadow to expand their dominion across Middle-earth.

{=taom_str_culture_description.aserai}The Haradrim, warriors of the southern deserts, are a fierce and resilient people allied with Sauron. Known for their exotic war beasts and skilled cavalry, they march to war under crimson banners. Proud and deeply rooted in their traditions, they bring the savagery of the desert to the battlefields of Middle-earth.

{=taom_str_culture_description.sturgia}The Bardings of Dale, descendants of Bard the Bowman, are a proud and industrious people living in the shadow of Erebor. Renowned for their skilled archers and disciplined warriors, they safeguard their thriving city and the trade routes of the north. United by a strong sense of community and honor, the Bardings stand firm against the darkness threatening their lands.

{=taom_str_culture_description.erebor}The noble Dwarves of Erebor, are renowned for their craftsmanship, resilience, and pride. From their halls in the Lonely Mountain, they forge mighty weapons and treasures of unmatched beauty. Clad in mail and armed with axes, they defend their kin with steadfast courage, seeking to reclaim their legacy and preserve their heritage against all who threaten it.

{=taom_str_culture_description.rivendell}Rivendell, the Last Homely House, is a refuge of wisdom and beauty led by Lord Elrond. Nestled in the Misty Mountains, its people are loremasters and guardians of Middle-earth's ancient knowledge. The Elves of Rivendell offer counsel and aid to those who stand against the darkness, preserving the light of hope and unity.

{=taom_str_culture_description.mirkwood}The Wood-Elves of Mirkwood, led by King Thranduil, are guardians of the vast and mysterious forest. Known for their agility and mastery of the bow, they blend into the shadows, striking with precision and grace. Their realm is one of beauty and peril, protected by the resolve of its warriors and the timeless wisdom of their king. Fiercely independent, the Elves of Mirkwood fight to preserve their forest against encroaching darkness.

{=taom_str_culture_description.lothlorien}The Galadhrim of Lothlórien, dwellers of the Golden Wood, are an ethereal and noble people led by Lady Galadriel and Lord Celeborn. Masters of archery and woodland warfare, they guard their enchanted realm with unmatched skill. Their loyalty to their kin and homeland is unwavering, and their subtle magic preserves Lothlórien as a sanctuary of hope and light amidst the growing shadow.

{=taom_str_culture_description.isengard}The armies of Isengard, led by Saruman the White, are a formidable force of Uruk-hai and mercenaries. Forged in the fires of industry, their weapons and armor are crafted for destruction. The forces of Isengard march to war with ruthless efficiency, bent on conquest and domination.

{=taom_str_culture_description.gundabad}The Orcs of Gundabad, residing in the mist-shrouded mountains, are a brutal and savage force. Led by their warlords, they wage endless raids on neighboring lands. Driven by hatred and cruelty, they are relentless in their quest to dominate the north.

{=taom_str_culture_description.umbar}The Corsairs of Umbar, seafaring raiders and master sailors, are a ruthless and cunning people allied with Sauron. Known for their swift ships and relentless naval warfare, they strike fear into the coastlines of Middle-earth. Proud of their maritime heritage, they bring the chaos of the seas to the land, raiding and pillaging in the name of their dark alliances.

{=taom_str_culture_description.dolguldur}The minions of Dol Guldur, under the command of the Necromancer, are a dark and sinister force. Hidden within the corrupted forest of Mirkwood, they employ treachery and shadow to weaken their enemies. Orcs, wargs, and other foul creatures march forth to spread fear and decay across Middle-earth.

{=taom_str_culture_description.gondor}The Gondorians, descendants of the Númenórean exiles, are the proud stewards of the greatest kingdom of Men in Middle-earth. Known for their towering stone fortresses and unwavering courage, Gondor is a bastion of hope against the looming shadow of Mordor. Its disciplined armies, comprised of valiant infantry, skilled archers, and mounted knights, stand as a shield for all free peoples. Guided by noble stewards and captains, the Gondorians hold fast to their traditions, unyielding in their duty to protect the realm and its legacy.

{=taom_str_culture_description.mordor}The armies of Mordor, forged in the shadow of Mount Doom, are a relentless force of darkness commanded by Sauron, the Dark Lord. Comprised of orcs, trolls, and wicked men, they march to war under the burning Eye, sowing fear and destruction. These legions are driven by cruelty and servitude, wielding jagged blades and crude armor. Bound by Sauron's iron will, the forces of Mordor are a deadly tide seeking to engulf all of Middle-earth in shadow.

{=taom_shaghana_desc}Shaghâna is the eastern reach of Harad, a land of sun-scorched steppes and ancient fortresses. Its nine tribal clans are fierce warriors, bound together by oath and blood, striking fear into those who dare oppose them.

{=aom_shaghana_desc}The Shaghâna are a fierce tribal people of the eastern Harad steppes, renowned as relentless raiders and skilled horsemen. Bound by oath and clan, they answer to their Taskral and serve the dark designs of Sauron from their sun-scorched fortresses.

{=taom_abanissa_desc}Âbanissa lies in the deep south of Harad, a realm of humid jungles and ancient stone dynasties. The great Houses of Âbanissa command fearsome war-beasts and armies of disciplined warriors, their power answerable to none but Sauron himself.

{=aom_abanissa_desc}The great Houses of Âbanissa rule the deep south of Harad, a land of humid jungles, ancient stone palaces and towering war-beasts. Their armies march beneath banners of dynasty, commanding respect and terror across the southern lands.

{=TAOM_ghilman_text}The Serpent Guard are mounted soldiers in the service of the Serpentlord of Near Harad. Bred in the saddle on the rolling plains south of the Ephel Dúath, they are unmatched as horse-archers in all of Middle-earth's southern lands. In times of peace between Harad and Mordor, the Guard hires its services to Haradrim lords and to any other power rich enough to afford their golden fee.

{=TAOM_legion_text}The Grey Company are the last organised brotherhood of the Dúnedain Rangers, descendants of the kings of Arnor who lost their kingdom ages ago. They ride across the North without a home of their own, keeping the peace in lands that have forgotten their names. Though their first loyalty is to the line of Elendil, they take contracts from lords across Middle-earth when their wandering brings them through civilised lands.

{=TAOM_skolderbrotva_text}The Axemen of Erebor are veterans of King Thorin's battles who found peacetime ill-suited to their temperament. Trained in the close-quarter fighting of the Dwarven halls — shield wall, short axe, mattock — they are formidable on any terrain but excel in the mountain passes that connect Erebor to the kingdoms of men. They take contracts from any who can afford their fee, but will not raise an axe against Erebor or Rivendell.

{=TAOM_company_text}The Corsair Blades are veteran sea-fighters from the harbours of Umbar who have taken to selling their skills on land. They fight as crossbowmen — the preferred arm of shipboard warfare — and are as comfortable in a siege as they are on a rolling deck. Their captain, a scarred Númenórean exile, keeps them to their contracts with iron discipline, knowing that their reputation is their most valuable cargo.

{=TAOM_beni_zilal_text}The Blind Eye is a brotherhood of smugglers, fences, and hired killers operating across the coasts of Harad and the deep desert. They are said to descend from a cult of assassins who served a forgotten Haradrim king, and their methods — poison, shadow, and the leveraging of secrets — remain unchanged. Lords who wish to quietly remove a rival, or merchants who need cargo moved without customs inspection, know where to leave a gold coin and a sealed letter.

{=TAOM_wolfskins_text}The Variag Ravagers are war-bands of young Variag warriors from the steppes of Khand who spend their early manhood in a state of ritual warfare: they may own no cooked food, sleep under no permanent roof, and take no mercy. While most eventually return to the settled life of their clans, some never do, and these form the Ravagers — outlaws who prey on the roads of Khand and raid across its borders into Harad and Gondor.

{=TAOM_brotherhood_text}The Dunlending Reavers are the broken remnant of a hill-clan that once dwelt in the valleys now ruled by the Rohirrim. Their grandfathers were driven from fertile land into the rocky heights, and they have nursed that bitterness into a raider's philosophy: everything taken from a southron or a king's man is merely the restoration of what was stolen. In practice they are brigands, but dangerous ones who know every goat-track through the hills.

{=TAOM_hidden_hand_text}The Mouth's Servants are the Eyes of Barad-dûr operating beyond the Black Gate — informants, enforcers, and spies embedded among the peoples bordering Mordor. Where Sauron's armies cannot yet reach, these agents collect tribute and silence dissent. They work through bribery, blackmail, and quiet murder, ensuring that no conspiracy against the Dark Lord takes root before it is uprooted and crushed.

{=TAOM_lakepike_text}The Wreckers of the Long Lake live in the reed-beds and rotting old jetties of the Long Lake's shadowed shores, far from the respectable lights of Esgaroth. They make their living by luring barges onto hidden shoals with false lanterns, then stripping the cargo and selling it through fences in the town itself. Despite the efforts of the Lake-town Master and the Dale merchants, the Wreckers have too many friends in the dockside taverns to be easily driven out.

{=TAOM_embers_text}The Cult of the Lidless Eye is a secret society rooted in the Black Númenórean tradition, venerating Sauron as a god-king who will restore his faithful to glory when he rises again. They recruit among the dispossessed of Dunland and the forgotten corners of the realm, promising divine favour and earthly power. In truth, their leaders answer to agents of Barad-dûr, and their cell-based structure makes them nearly impossible for any lord's justice to eradicate.

{=TAOM_jawwal_text}The Sand-Riders are the nomadic desert clans of the deep Harad interior, masters of the waterless wastes between the Ephel Dúath and the distant southern sea. They range across routes known only to themselves, demanding tribute from any caravan bold enough to cross their territory. The settled lords of Near Harad treat them as a nuisance; the Sand-Riders consider the settled lords thieves who stole what the desert had already given freely.

{=TAOM_karakhuzaits_text}The Wild Easterlings are the unconquered steppe clans of the Sea of Rhûn, who have resisted the authority of every lord who has tried to bring them to heel — Rhûn chieftain, Mordor lieutenant, and King of Dale alike. They range across the grasslands east of the Celduin, rounding up horses, raiding flocks, and collecting road tribute from any caravan foolish enough to cross their steppe without an armed escort.

{=TAOM_forest_people_text}The Drúedain, known to Men as Woses or the Wild Men of the Woods, are an ancient people who dwell in the deep forest of Drúadan and the hidden valleys of the White Mountains. They clear ground with fire, grow what they need on the ash-rich soil, and move on when the land is spent — a way of life the settled peoples of Middle-earth have never understood and never bothered to. The Drúedain want no lord, pay no tax, and ask only to be left to the forest's silence.

{=TAOM_eleftheroi_text}The Beornings are the great woodmen who dwell in the vale of the Anduin between the Misty Mountains and Mirkwood, led by the skin-changers of Beorn's line. They allow no Orc to cross their territory, charge a toll at the Ford of Carrock to fund their watch, and answer to no king in Middle-earth. Though they will trade and talk with Elves and Dwarves, any army that marches through their forest without leave will find that the Beornings have very large teeth.
{=taom_war_blocked}These kingdoms are bound by an unbreakable alliance.
